content.text: Pair 1 names only the high-level method ("matrix method") and omits every substantive element of the key: the spread over the interpolated Treasury curve derived from comparable public securities, the quarterly Valuation Committee illiquidity premium (15–40 bps), the covenant/make-whole/security/subordination adjustments, and the discounting of scheduled cash flows at the resulting yield. That is a missing-required-element case, not a formatting difference.

pairs.note: Answer states only the high-level label ('matrix method') and omits the substance the key requires: the spread over the interpolated U.S. Treasury curve based on comparable public securities of the same/comparable issuer, the quarterly Valuation Committee illiquidity premium of 15-40 bps, the adjustments for covenants, make-whole, security and subordination, and discounting scheduled cash flows at the resulting yield. Missing required elements rather than mere brevity of wording.
